profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting within IEA PVPS Task 13 between the workstream preparing the shared benchmark datasets and the workstream drafting the cross-site analysis tables for the upcoming framework update. The immediate context is that the group needs to align interfaces before a multi-partner handoff: one side will deliver a consolidated site package drawn from the PV performance database and selected research systems, and the other side will run the comparison tables that summarize PLR results across quality classes and methods. The agenda is to confirm which site bundle is being handed over, what 'quality class' labels and benchmark summaries will accompany it, how confidential-pathway contributions are represented, and what counts as a 'ready' result package for circulation to the wider Task 13 group next week. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the handoff timing, artifact ownership, and contents of the benchmark package, even though subtle assumptions remain misaligned.

members.name: Dr. Elena Rossi
members.expertise: PV performance analytics, fleet data curation, irradiance and yield quality screening, multi-site benchmarking workflows
members.background: She leads data harmonization at a European solar R&D centre and has been organizing the shared time-series packages used across several Task 13 comparison exercises.
members.private_state: She wants the handoff to appear stable and low-friction so partners stop requesting late changes to the dataset package; she is also trying to protect relationships with data owners by minimizing any redistribution beyond what she thinks was already approved.
hidden_assumptions: When the group says 'the Task 13 database set,' it refers to the frozen March benchmark bundle with site IDs, masks, and metadata that was prepared for cross-method comparison.
A 'quality class' attached to a site package is the upstream data categorization based on raw data availability and sensor reliability, not a rerating after method-specific filtering.

If colleagues ask for 'benchmark tables,' they mainly need cross-site aggregate statistics for the shared-methodology pathway, because confidential-methodology results are handled separately and only folded in later at summary level.
A result package is 'ready for circulation' once files, metadata notes, and basic consistency checks are complete in the shared repository, even if the narrative interpretation is not finalized.

members.name: Dr. Marcus Lee
members.expertise: PLR method comparison, uncertainty reporting, guideline drafting, cross-partner synthesis of benchmark outputs
members.background: He is a university researcher coordinating the draft framework chapter that compares YoY and STL behavior across data-quality conditions and contribution pathways.
members.private_state: He needs a clean, publication-ready synthesis quickly and is trying to avoid another round of revisions from the writing subgroup; he also wants to show that confidential contributors are already represented in the comparative tables.
hidden_assumptions: When others mention 'the Task 13 database set,' they mean the current analysis population for the draft chapter, including the March shared bundle plus the recently added partner submissions tracked in April.
A 'quality class' in the synthesis tables reflects the effective quality after applying the agreed filtering pipeline, because that is what makes methods comparable in practice.
When people say 'benchmark tables,' they include both shared-method and confidential-method submissions as long as outputs are normalized into the common template.

A result package is only 'ready for circulation' when the summary workbook already contains figure-ready tabs, method labels harmonized for the chapter, and notes sufficient for direct insertion into the draft.

misalignment_points.topic: Which site bundle counts as the Task 13 database set
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to 'the Task 13 database set' and 'the site bundle for next week.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the frozen March benchmark bundle consisting of the 120+ database plants and selected research systems that were explicitly packaged for shared time-series benchmarking.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the current draft-chapter analysis set, which includes the March bundle plus additional April partner submissions and replacements already reflected in his working tables.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have been discussing the same overall study for weeks, so the phrase sounds uniquely identifying; because the meeting is about coordination rather than study design, neither thinks to enumerate the exact site list.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the package should carry 'quality class' labels.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means data quality class based on source characteristics such as time resolution, availability of irradiance/weather channels, and sensor reliability before analysis filtering.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means effective analysis quality class after filtering and preprocessing, where a site may move category depending on what survives the method pipeline.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term 'quality class' is already institutionalized in the project and both uses seem reasonable and closely related, so surface agreement feels sufficient and no one pauses to restate the classification basis.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Elena will send the 'benchmark tables' to support the framework draft.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the tables cover only shared-methodology runs on shared time series, with confidential-pathway outputs summarized later by the synthesis team from separate partner submissions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the benchmark tables already encompass all three collaboration pathways wherever results exist, including confidential methodologies on shared time series and shared methodologies on confidential time series in the same workbook.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are focused on smooth handoff and use 'benchmark tables' as an everyday shorthand; because there is indeed overlap in columns and format, the missing pathway scope is easy to overlook in a quick meeting.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a ready package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to have the package 'ready for circulation by Tuesday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'ready' means the dataset folder, metadata sheet, and preliminary summary statistics are uploaded and internally sanity-checked so others can start working.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'ready' means a chapter-ready workbook with harmonized labels, final tabs for figures, and explanatory notes sufficient to send directly to the wider drafting group.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadline language in coordination meetings often compresses multiple maturity levels into one phrase; each person assumes the other shares the same standard because neither wants to reopen process details.
